candidate: Exact BF16 block base-plus-delta packing for all batch-1 decode projections
scope: Qwen3.5-0.8B, RTX 4060 Laptop SM89, batch-1 decode

correctness.note: FP32 reduction order can still change intermediate outputs even though every BF16 weight bit is reconstructed exactly.

scalar_unpack_cold_stream.protocol: Rotate every layer weight in each group; every included working set exceeds the 32 MiB L2; 100 paired warmups, 7 repeats, 5 iterations per sample, eight launch schedules.

tensorcore_unpack_screen.protocol: Hoist block metadata per row/tile, reconstruct exact BF16, pad M=1 to M=16 and use Tensor Core dot; seven bounded schedules.

current_frontier_profile.warning: Profiler timings are perturbative and are used for opportunity ranking and reachability, not as production latency.

roofline_context.interpretation: The remaining strict BF16 search space is narrow: even an impossible deletion of all non-weight time is bounded near 1.16x at the measured bandwidth.

why_lmhead_differs: The single 508.6 MB lm_head is a large DRAM stream whose regular bit reconstruction can be hidden by reduced traffic. Backbone projections are much smaller and repeated; cuBLAS already uses efficient shape-specific reductions, so scalar integer unpack or padded Tensor Core work becomes the bottleneck.
reopen_condition: Reopen only with a native compressed-BF16 dot instruction, an unpack path that beats cuBLAS on cold rotating weights for every material shape, or a producer-consumer architecture that eliminates additional weight/input traffic and predicts at least 3% whole-step gain.
